human_tolerance.notes: In urban areas its dens are almost entirely in buildings, particularly in winter; it occasionally raids poultry and damages car wiring (Wikipedia, English).

phases.name: mating
phases.note: Oestrus and copulation June to August (French Wikipedia; English Wikipedia gives June-July).

phases.name: young
phases.note: Parturition late March to early April; young are indistinguishable from adults in early July.

inat.note: Permissive tier A (cc0, cc-by) total for this place is 100, below min_obs 300, so the tool widened to tier C (adds cc-by-sa, cc-by-nc, cc-by-nc-sa). The NC iNaturalist data contributes 749 of 50192 records and is therefore a non-commercial input to the FR curve. A GBIF-only permissive curve is kept in query.gbif_only_fixed_monthly.

gbif.excluded_dataset_title: Répartition de différentes espèces de petits et méso carnivores en France (ONCFS et coll.)
gbif.excluded_dataset_reason: All 9,271 of its records in this query carry placeholder event dates on 1 January (2015, 2016 and 2017 in a 300-record sample); 3,861 of them fall in January, which produced a spurious January peak in the tool's raw GBIF curve. Removed from both the species and mammal-class monthly counts.

query.exclusions_applied_by: Recomputed from the fetch_activity.py functions (share_curve, mean_curves, finalize_curve) with the excluded dataset subtracted; the raw tool output is kept below for audit.

taxonomy.note: GBIF species match usageKey 5218887, rank SPECIES, status ACCEPTED, family Mustelidae, authorship (Erxleben, 1777). ITIS TSN 621941 valid, same authorship. Checked 2026-11-01.

external.note: iNaturalist taxon 41800 (species rank, active, Stone Marten) via Wikidata P3151 and the iNaturalist taxa API; GBIF key via Wikidata P846; ITIS TSN via Wikidata P815 (621941).

common_names.note: 'stone marten' is the alternative English name given in the lead of the English article; Wikidata's English label is 'beech marten'. fr 'Fouine' and de 'Steinmarder' are the Wikidata labels.

conservation.note: Wikidata P141 = least concern (Q211005); the English article's lead gives the same IUCN category.

range.note: Country list derived from the English article (native from Spain and Portugal through central and southern Europe, Aegean islands; absent from the British Isles, Scandinavian Peninsula, Finland, northern Baltic); German article (central and southern Europe); French article (species present in France). BE is listed on GBIF distributions (Waarnemingen.be, NATIVE). Only these countries were confirmed; the list is partial, not exhaustive. introduced US: the English article's North America section describes a feral population from fur-farm escapes in Wisconsin.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Walk: 'moves by creeping in a polecat-like manner'. Climb: 'a skilled climber in heavily forested areas'. Swim: 'a skilled swimmer'. Gallop is authored for the flee gait (judgement; the English article does not name a gait). Climb and Swim are not reachable in the shared program (see behavior); they are declared because the animal does them.

traits.skin.note: Fur: coarse guard hairs and underfur (English article, Description).

traits.nest_type.note: Nests in naturally occurring rock fissures and clefts, stone structures, buildings and tree holes; does not dig burrows. Mapped to Cavity.

traits.perching.note: Climbs trees but is not a perching animal in the schema sense; set false.

traits.mass_kg.note: Unweighted mean of four sex-by-season midpoints from the English article: males 1.7-1.8 kg (winter) and 2.0-2.1 kg (summer); females 1.1-1.3 kg (winter) and 1.4-1.5 kg (summer). Midpoints 1.75, 2.05, 1.2, 1.45; mean 1.6 kg.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: Lowest female winter weight (1.1 kg) to highest male summer weight (2.1 kg), English article.

traits.length_m.note: Schema length is nose to tail tip. Mean head-body length 0.47 m (male 430-590 mm, female 380-470 mm; midpoints 510 and 425 mm, averaged) plus mean tail length 0.27 m (male 250-320 mm, female 230-275 mm; midpoints 285 and 252.5 mm, averaged): 0.74 m. Not the ADW 40-54 cm figure, which is a different measurement.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Non-commercial last resort. ADW Lifespan/Longevity: 'Average longevity of M. foina in its natural habitat is 3 years.' Typical wild lifespan; ADW cites no source for it. The 10-year wild maximum and 18-year captive figure are not the same statistic and are not used. Permissive search (bounded, 2026-11-01): English, French and German Wikipedia articles give no lifespan; Wikidata has no life-expectancy claim; AnAge (genomics.senescence.info) gives only a captive maximum of 18.2 years, and its licence was not verified, so it is not used. Peeva 2017 (ZooNotes, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.12658603) is CC BY-NC-ND 3.0, rejected for ND. Ruette et al. 2014 (J Zool, 10.1111/jzo.12201) has a Wiley licence without an open CC grant, so it is not used. Blocker for a permissive replacement: a licensed source for mean wild lifespan.

traits.diet.note: Authored allocation. The sources give only presence and qualitative shares: omnivorous; plant food predominates in winter (English) and fruit in summer and autumn (German); rodents, birds and eggs, insects, frogs and carrion (German); the English article states more plant food than the pine marten, and that males take larger live prey while females eat small prey and carrion more often. No percentage is sourced. Fruit 0.35, invertebrate 0.15, vertebrate 0.40 and carrion 0.10 are judgement; treat as low-confidence.

traits.social.note: 'Wie die meisten Marder sind Steinmarder Einzelgänger' (solitary, territorial outside mating). Group size 1 is the adult solitary state.

traits.activity_pattern.note: 'mainly a crepuscular and nocturnal animal' (English), 'principalement crépusculaire et nocturne' (French). Nocturnal chosen as the schema pattern for the nocturnal foraging executed by the program; a Spanish study cited on the English page records most activity 6 pm to midnight.

traits.defense.note: Judgement from a mustelid that is an evasive forager rather than a defensive one; the article describes no specific threat response.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement, not sourced. Set to 0.6 to match the mid-range value used for other ground-living carnivores in this kit.

habitat.use.note: Authored split. The article describes it as more terrestrial and less arboreal than the pine marten, typically hunting on the ground, and as a skilled climber in forests: ground 0.9, arboreal 0.1 is judgement.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Rests in fissures and clefts, stone structures, buildings and tree holes: mapped to the 'cavity' resource tag.

habitat.resources.note: Resource weights are authored and follow the diet allocation above. The shelter weight is 1.0 as for the fox record. Fruit has no month restriction because the English article says plant food predominates in winter, so year-round use is the supported reading.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Urban dens are almost entirely in buildings, particularly in winter; poultry raids and car damage ('Automarder' in German). Exploiter is the schema's closest category: urban animal that uses buildings and gardens.

seasonal.note: Mating June to August (French article) and June to July (English article). Parturition late March to early April, average litter 3-7 kits (English); 3-4 on average (French). Kits indistinguishable from adults in early July (English). Strategy is year-round activity: no dormancy is described in either article.

vocalizations.note: No vocalisation data sourced; the list is intentionally empty. Not claimed.

look.note: Block-model colours and proportions are judgement. The sourced features are the white throat patch that extends to the forelegs and the pale nose (English article, Description); the browser preview is required for visual checks.

behavior.note: Shared program fsm-ground-forager-v1 fits a ground-hunting mustelid that forages on foot and rests in shelter by day. Limits: the program cannot climb or swim; the animal's arboreal and aquatic skills are not executed. Food tag small_vertebrate reflects the ground-hunting description; fruit and invertebrates are represented as resources only.

activity.note: Observation-based curve for FR: mean of iNaturalist share (tier C, incl. NC; 749 records) and GBIF share (tier A, CC0/CC BY, 49,443 records after excluding the placeholder-dated ONCFS dataset). Raw tool curve retained in query.raw_tool_monthly. Observation frequency is only a proxy for activity: the curve is high in winter and low in summer, which may reflect observer effort, winter dens in buildings and road or house contacts, not solely activity.
